reference: No matching GNU CLI is available: crontab manages tables, while GNU cron/crond has no command that prints the next matching epoch. cron next expectations below use the documented five-field/nickname contract and independently calculated UTC Unix timestamps. cron run --once expectations use the documented private-spool/state behavior and relative fixture markers; these are contract checks, not GNU parity.
coverage: Bash type/help metadata for the cron builtin.
cron next minute steps, leap-day calendar traversal, Vixie day-of-month/day-of-week OR semantics, named month/day fields, and a documented nickname.
Rejection of @reboot by cron next, as the help text says it is not a cron next schedule.
cron run --once creation and persistence of a private spool/state file using relative fixture paths.
cron run --once execution and removal of a due atjob while retaining a future atjob, with marker files confined to the fixture directory.
exclusions: No cron-specific parity cases are claimed because there is no matching GNU next-time CLI; unrelated utility parity would not test cron.
Long-running daemon polling, @reboot dispatch, reload/shutdown, and system-crontab privilege dropping are deferred.
Bash type/help and command help/version cases are metadata only and do not count as operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Checks Bash's builtin type result and the documented run, next, and @reboot help topics. The required phrases come from cron_doc in the documented source.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t cron) == builtin ]] || exit 10
cron_docs=$(help cron)
[[ $cron_docs == *"cron run [--once] [--interval SEC]"* && $cron_docs == *"cron next [--from EPOCH]"* && $cron_docs == *"@reboot runs once when daemon mode starts"* ]] || exit 11
printf 'builtin and documented help are available\n'
cases.stdout: builtin and documented help are available

cases.purpose: Bash help -s prints the builtin's one-line usage synopsis. The expected synopsis is the short_doc field declared in cron_struct in the documented source.
cases.stdout: cron: cron run [--once] [--interval SEC] | cron next [--from EPOCH] {MIN HOUR DOM MONTH DOW|@daily}

cases.purpose: At 2023-11-14 22:13:20 UTC, */15 next matches 22:15:00 UTC. The expected epoch 1700000100 is independently derived from the UTC calendar and minute-step rule.
Checks sparse calendar traversal to 2024-02-29 04:30:00 UTC; its independently calculated Unix timestamp is 1709181000.
With both day fields restricted, standard Vixie cron semantics match either the 13th or Monday. From 2023-11-14, the next match is Monday 2023-11-20 00:00 UTC (1700438400).
Checks documented JAN and MON field names. The first matching January Monday after 2023-11-14 is 2024-01-01 04:00 UTC (1704081600).
Checks the documented @daily nickname from one second after the Unix epoch; the next midnight is epoch 86400.
cron next rejects @reboot with usage status and a visible diagnostic; no daemon starts.

Runs only cron run --once with relative private paths. The documented state minute for epoch 1700000000 is floor(epoch/60)=28333333; the script also asserts that the spool subdirectories and configured output directory exist.
cases.script:
BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR=spool BASHCRON_OUTPUT_DIR=out BASHCRON_ETC_DIR=etc BASHCRON_CROND_DIR=cron.d BASHCRON_NOW_EPOCH=1700000000 BASHCRON_STATE_FILE=state cron run --once
[[ -d spool/atjobs && -d spool/tabs && -d out && -f state ]] || exit 10
IFS= read -r saved_minute < state
[[ $saved_minute == 28333333 ]] || exit 11
printf 'minute=%s directories=ready\n' "$saved_minute"

cases.purpose: Uses a private spool and fixed epoch to run a due fixture job, remove its consumed .job file, and retain a job scheduled one second in the future. Both job payloads only write relative marker files.
cases.script:
BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR=spool BASHCRON_OUTPUT_DIR=out BASHCRON_ETC_DIR=etc BASHCRON_CROND_DIR=cron.d BASHCRON_NOW_EPOCH=1700000000 cron run --once
printf '%s\n' '# run_at=1700000000' "printf 'ran\\n' > due-marker" > spool/atjobs/due.job
printf '%s\n' '# run_at=1700000001' "printf 'ran\\n' > future-marker" > spool/atjobs/future.job
BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR=spool BASHCRON_OUTPUT_DIR=out BASHCRON_ETC_DIR=etc BASHCRON_CROND_DIR=cron.d BASHCRON_NOW_EPOCH=1700000000 cron run --once
[[ -f due-marker && ! -e spool/atjobs/due.job && -f spool/atjobs/future.job && ! -e future-marker ]] || exit 10
IFS= read -r due_result < due-marker
[[ $due_result == ran ]] || exit 11
printf 'due=ran future=waiting\n'

cases.purpose: Long-lived polling, @reboot execution, clock catch-up across polls, reload, and shutdown behavior.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM or purpose-built mock clock and child-process harness to keep cron run alive, advance time deterministically, inspect @reboot and catch-up dispatch, and deliver reload/shutdown signals only to that private process. This suite does not run a daemon or signal fixtures.

cases.purpose: System crontab dispatch under root with a real USER-column privilege transition, including failure refusal.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with an isolated account database and controlled root privilege, or a reviewed syscall mock for getpwnam/initgroups/setgid/setuid. User/account changes and privilege manipulation are out of scope here; the test must verify the selected uid and that a failed drop never executes the command.
